compiled_state.title: [llm-review-schema-correction]: synthetic fallback_exhausted is removed by correction, count-equality check then fails -> CI blocks merge with synthetic schema_error
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview
Observed on PR #167 (https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/167), llm-review job 76343247603 (run 25970902666). The llm-review CI workflow failed with a synthetic \`schema_error\` finding, fail-closed, even though no real review finding existed on the trivial 4-line diff.

## Sequence
1. Primary reviewer (code-reviewer-standard / claude-sonnet-4-6) returned a non-JSON response: \`ERROR: LLM returned non-JSON response (length=1818); cannot parse as findings.\`
2. Fallback chain exhausted; dispatch.py emitted a single synthetic \`fallback_exhausted\` pseudo-finding (per its DD3 contract — dispatch.py:9, 50, 327).
3. Schema correction loop ran; it correctly recognized the \`fallback_exhausted\` entry as a meta/synthetic finding (not a real code-review finding) and removed it. Resulting findings array length = 0.
4. dispatch.py:993-998 count-equality check fires: \`finding count mismatch: got 0, expected 1\`. The loop treats this as an error and retries; the retry also returns 0 findings (correctly — the original was a single fallback marker); after attempts exhausted, the loop emits a synthetic \`schema_error\` finding with severity 'important' and the runner fails CI (exit 1).

## Expected Behavior
When the original findings array contains only synthetic-type entries (\`fallback_exhausted\`, \`specialist_error\`, \`parse_error\` — already enumerated as the synthetic-type set at plugins/dso/scripts/validate-review-output.sh:351), schema correction validly producing 0 findings should NOT be treated as a count mismatch. The count-equality check should compare counts of REAL findings (excluding synthetic types) on both sides, OR the synthetic-only original should short-circuit before the count check fires.

## Actual Behavior
plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/dispatch.py:993-998 compares raw lengths:
\`\`\`
if len(attempt_findings) != len(original_findings):
    last_error = (
        f"finding count mismatch: got {len(attempt_findings)}, "
        f"expected {len(original_findings)}"
    )
    continue
\`\`\`
No exemption for synthetic-type original entries; correction's valid 0-count is treated as failure.

## Reproduction
- Trigger the primary reviewer to return non-JSON (occurs on ~small-diff PRs where the model emits prose instead of structured JSON; see ci-llm-review run 25970902666 turn-0 stderr 'Anthropic cache_read_input_tokens did not increase on turn 1 (prev=16325, current=16325)')
- dispatch.py emits the \`fallback_exhausted\` pseudo-finding
- Schema correction (any attempt count) removes the pseudo-finding -> 0 findings remain
- dispatch.py:995 reports count mismatch -> retries exhausted -> synthetic schema_error -> CI fail

## Impact
CI fail-closed on infrastructure-only failure: blocks merge of correct, finding-free diffs whenever the primary reviewer's first response is non-JSON. Re-running the workflow may succeed (different LLM response) but the user experiences spurious merge blocks on trivial PRs. Observed: PR #167, a 4-line typo fix (CLAUDE_SESSION_ID -> CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID), blocked by this exact path.

## Proposed Fix Direction (not implementing here)
At dispatch.py:993, before the length comparison, filter both sides to non-synthetic types using the synthetic-types set from validate-review-output.sh:351 (\`{'specialist_error', 'fallback_exhausted', 'parse_error'}\`). Compare counts of real findings only. If the original was entirely synthetic and the correction yields 0 real findings, that is the correct outcome — do not retry, do not emit schema_error.

## Related
- dispatch.py:9, 50, 327 (DD3 fallback_exhausted contract)
- validate-review-output.sh:349-351 (synthetic-types set)
- Recent commit db971905a4 'docs(tests): document severity demotion rationale in schema_correction docstring (eac2-16ff)' — related work in same area
